# Example Output — Marketing Email Campaign

*Generated by applying the Marketing Email Campaign skill to `example-input.md`.*

---

## 1. Template

- **Card fixed with the fluid-hybrid pattern:** `width="100%" style="width:100%; max-width:600px"` inside an MSO conditional ghost table pinned at 600 for desktop Outlook (see `reference.md`). The old `width:600px; max-width:100%` sizing was the overflow cause — percentage max-width is circular inside nested tables and resolved back to 600px on phones.
- **Footer rebuilt as strip + solid cell:** the wave graphic is now a full-width `<img>` whose bottom edge ends flat in `#1A2B3C`, followed by a `bgcolor="#1A2B3C"` cell holding the footer text — no more collisions at any wrap width.
- **Header art** drawn programmatically from the palette with the logo composited and the "Northwind Analytics" wordmark baked in Sora; the course subline stays live text so future intakes can change it. Google Fonts link included (benefits Apple Mail; others get the fallback stack).

## 2. Preview config

- `www.example.com/email-preview` given a per-route CSP allowing `'unsafe-inline'` styles (the site-wide `style-src 'self'` was stripping every inline style — real sends were never affected), `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, beacon excluded.

## 3. Compliance block

- Footer carries the sender identification line ("Northwind Analytics Pty Ltd, <city>") and the unsubscribe link.
- Unsubscribe: branded page confirms on GET, POSTs on click; endpoint idempotent, token opaque and unlogged, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers on every send; suppression list enforced at send time.
- Cold-outreach basis noted; no tracking pixels — consistent with the published no-tracking stance.

## 4. Seed-test report

| Check | Gmail | Outlook.com | Corporate tenant |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPF / DKIM / DMARC | pass / pass / pass | pass / pass / pass | pass / pass / pass |
| `multipart/alternative` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `List-Unsubscribe` headers | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Single subject / greeting | ✗ → fixed | — | — |
| Preheader independent | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

Fix applied: the send tool prepends "Hi <name>," — greeting removed from body copy; blank-name render checked ("Hi," acceptable). **Second seed re-run clean** — the campaign now validates the exact construction that will send.

## 5. Warm-up run sheet

| Batch | Size | Composition | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–3 | 20/day | warmest private-practice contacts | manual advance after signal review |
| 4+ | 25–30/day | remainder, ≤5/day to the shared government domain, batch filled from next group | pause on bounce cluster |

Watch between batches: replies (answer them), bounces (cluster = pause), complaints (most damaging — frictionless unsubscribe is the diversion). Manual send-next-batch button; no scheduler until auto-pause guardrails exist.

## 6. Send-tool spec

Vendored template, header/footer locked; compose = subject, preheader, constrained rich-text body, 0–2 CTA pills (https on `example.com` domains only); CSV recipient groups with validation, case-insensitive dedupe, visible counts; `[TEST]`-prefixed test sends before an explicit confirmed real send; per-recipient audit storing the exact rendered email; open/click tracking disabled (no-tracking stance).

## 7. Delivery audit

Per-recipient rendered copies in the tool's audit table. One corporate-tenant seed landed in junk: `X-Microsoft-Antispam-Mailbox-Delivery` showed `dest:J ... OFR:SpamFilterAuthJ` — authenticated-but-junked on new-domain reputation, expected during warm-up; the recipient's Not-Junk click flipped later seeds to `TrustedSenderList`. High-value public-sector targets flagged for personal one-to-one email from the org mailbox instead of the campaign path.
